label: Acts 18:1
text: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth.

label: Acts 18:2
text: He found a certain Jew named Aquila, a man of Pontus by race, who had recently come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome. He came to them,

label: Acts 18:3
text: and because he practiced the same trade, he lived with them and worked, for by trade they were tent makers.

label: Acts 18:4
text: He reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath, and persuaded Jews and Greeks.

label: Acts 18:5
text: But when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was compelled by the Spirit, testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.

label: Acts 18:6
text: When they opposed him and blasphemed, he shook out his clothing and said to them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am clean. From now on, I will go to the Gentiles!”

label: Acts 18:7
text: He departed there, and went into the house of a certain man named Justus, one who worshiped God, whose house was next door to the synagogue.

label: Acts 18:8
text: Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his house. Many of the Corinthians, when they heard, believed and were baptized.

label: Acts 18:9
text:
The Lord said to Paul in the night by a vision,
“Don’t be afraid, but speak and don’t be silent;

label: Acts 18:10
text: for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many people in this city.”

label: Acts 18:11
text: He lived there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

label: Acts 18:12
text: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat,

label: Acts 18:13
text: saying, “This man persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.”

label: Acts 18:14
text: But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If indeed it were a matter of wrong or of wicked crime, you Jews, it would be reasonable that I should bear with you;

label: Acts 18:15
text: but if they are questions about words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves. For I don’t want to be a judge of these matters.”

label: Acts 18:16
text: So he drove them from the judgment seat.

label: Acts 18:17
text: Then all the Greeks laid hold on Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. Gallio didn’t care about any of these things.

label: Acts 18:18
text:
Paul, having stayed after this many more days, took his leave of the brothers,
 and sailed from there for Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.

label: Acts 18:19
text: He came to Ephesus, and he left them there; but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.

label: Acts 18:20
text: When they asked him to stay with them a longer time, he declined;

label: Acts 18:21
text: but taking his leave of them, he said, “I must by all means keep this coming feast in Jerusalem, but I will return again to you if God wills.” Then he set sail from Ephesus.

label: Acts 18:22
text: When he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the assembly, and went down to Antioch.

label: Acts 18:23
text: Having spent some time there, he departed, and went through the region of Galatia, and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples.

label: Acts 18:24
text: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus. He was mighty in the Scriptures.

label: Acts 18:25
text: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, although he knew only the baptism of John.

label: Acts 18:26
text: He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside, and explained to him the way of God more accurately.

variants.reading: την οδον ('the way') instead of την οδον του θεου ('the way of God')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' lists for Acts 18:26: την οδον - D d gig; την οδον του θεου - P74, Sinaiticus, A, B, 33, 88 and others; την οδον του κυριου - E 1505 2495 l598; τον λογον του κυριου - 945 1739; την του θεου οδον - P Psi 049 0142 and the Byzantine text. The WEB follows the Alexandrian reading, carried by codex-sinaiticus and codex-vaticanus; the variant reading itself is carried by no manuscript node of this graph.

label: Acts 18:27
text: When he had determined to pass over into Achaia, the brothers encouraged him, and wrote to the disciples to receive him. When he had come, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace;

label: Acts 18:28
text: for he powerfully refuted the Jews, publicly showing by the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.

label: Aquila of Pontus
note: Jewish tentmaker 'of Pontus by race', expelled from Rome with his wife Priscilla by Claudius's edict; met Paul at Corinth (Acts 18:2-3) and worked with him; later at Ephesus (18:19, 26). Named again in 1 Corinthians 16:19, Romans 16:3-5 and 2 Timothy 4:19. No source outside the New Testament names him.

label: Priscilla (Prisca)
note: Wife of Aquila; with him a tentmaker, expelled from Rome by Claudius's edict, then at Corinth and Ephesus with Paul (Acts 18). Named again in 1 Corinthians 16:19, Romans 16:3-5 and 2 Timothy 4:19. No source outside the New Testament names her.

label: Justus (Titius Justus)
note: God-worshiper of Corinth whose house, next door to the synagogue, received Paul (Acts 18:7); later manuscripts add the nomen Titius. No source outside the New Testament names him.

label: Crispus
note: Ruler of the synagogue at Corinth who believed with all his house (Acts 18:8); 1 Corinthians 1:14 says Paul baptized him. No source outside the New Testament names him.

label: Lucius Junius Gallio Annaeanus
note: Roman senator, brother of Seneca; proconsul of Achaia when the Jews of Corinth brought Paul before the judgment seat (Acts 18:12-17). Claudius's Delphi letter names him 'my friend and proconsul'.

label: Sosthenes
note: Ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, beaten before the judgment seat while Gallio paid no attention (Acts 18:17); 1 Corinthians 1:1 names 'Sosthenes the brother' with Paul, possibly the same man. No independent source names him.

label: Apollos
note: Alexandrian Jew learned in the scriptures, instructed in the way of the Lord, active at Corinth while Paul was at Ephesus (Acts 18:24-19:1). No source outside the New Testament names him.

label: Paul (Saul of Tarsus)
note: First mention at Acts 7:58 as the young man at whose feet the witnesses laid their garments; later Acts chapters reuse this node.

label: Silas
note: Companion of Paul on the second journey (from Acts 15:22, a leading man of the Jerusalem assembly); shares the Philippi beating and imprisonment (Acts 16:19-40).

label: Timothy of Lystra
note: Disciple from Lystra; son of a believing Jewish mother and a Greek father (Acts 16:1); circumcised by Paul and joined the journey (16:3). No source outside the New Testament names him.

label: Pontus (region)
note: South-eastern Black Sea coast region of Asia Minor; Aquila's homeland at Acts 18:2.

label: Ephesus
note: Principal city of the Roman province of Asia; Paul's base for over two years (Acts 19:8-10).

label: Achaia (Roman province)
note: Senatorial province of southern Greece from 27 BCE; Gallio was its proconsul at Acts 18:12, and Apollos went over into it at Acts 18:27.

label: Galatia (region and Roman province)
note: Roman province from 25 BC, capital Ancyra; traversed at Acts 16:6.

label: Phrygia
note: Region of the west Anatolian plateau; traversed at Acts 16:6.
